claims.claim: 1. Reminder is standalone, with ScheduleType ONE_SHOT | CRON | STOCHASTIC and a UUID id.

evidence.quote: enum class ScheduleType { ONE_SHOT, CRON, STOCHASTIC }

claims.claim: 2. A reminder links to nothing else (no task, event or note id).

evidence.quote: * Single source of truth for a reminder — §15.3.

claims.claim: 3. Nag/escalation exists (repeat until acknowledged); say how it is configured.

evidence.quote: internal fun clampNagInterval(minutes: Int): Int = minutes.coerceIn(NAG_INTERVAL_MIN, NAG_INTERVAL_MAX)

claims.claim: 4. Snooze exists; say how it is stored.
5. 'Done' on a recurring reminder advances to the next fire; on a one-shot it archives the row.
6. nextFireAtEpochMillis is stored (precomputed), not derived at read time.
7. A reminder can have a time window (quiet hours / active hours) or per-reminder sound.

missed.fact: Claim 5 is only partly right. Done on a recurring reminder does NOT advance nextFireAtEpochMillis. It only clears snoozedUntilEpochMillis, and the next fire was already set by recordFired when the alarm fired. If Done comes from a snoozed state, nextFireAtEpochMillis still holds the snooze time, because snooze overwrites it and nothing restores the schedule. A recurring Done with no further occurrence archives the row, as a one-shot does.
The schema has a third enum besides ScheduleType: ReminderMode { EASE, SCHEDULE, ALERT }. It is a required field, `mode`, that the map did not list.

Complete Reminder column list (22): id, title, notes, scheduleType, cronExpr, stochasticDaysOfWeekMask, stochasticWindowStartMillisOfDay, stochasticWindowEndMillisOfDay, nextFireAtEpochMillis, mode, skinId, nagEnabled, soundUri, vibrationPattern, useExactAlarm, snoozedUntilEpochMillis, lastFiredAtEpochMillis, updatedAtEpochMillis, isArchived. That is 19 columns; I count 19, not 22. Fields outside the map: skinId (required String), vibrationPattern, useExactAlarm (default true) and notes.

isArchived carries three meanings in one column: soft delete (the sync tombstone), Done with nothing left, and a fired one-shot whose notification may still be showing. The class doc says never to read it as 'the episode is over'. A merge must treat it as both deletion and completion.

The window fields apply only to STOCHASTIC reminders, as a random-draw range with a day-of-week mask. They are not quiet hours or active hours for other types. The window is not checked anywhere else in the sources I searched.

soundUri is three-state: null = device default, empty string = explicit Silent, otherwise a content:// URI. vibrationPattern is also three-state: null = untouched, "0" = off, otherwise a preset pattern. A merge must not collapse null and empty.

The nag interval is global (an AppSettings DataStore key, default 5 min, clamped to 1..30), not a per-reminder column. Only the on/off flag is per reminder. Snooze length is a fixed 10 minutes and is not configurable.

Snooze overwrites nextFireAtEpochMillis and un-archives the row, so there is one field for both the scheduled fire and the snoozed fire. The original schedule time is lost for ONE_SHOT, and for recurring reminders until the next recordFired.
A second Room entity, SyncFileState, sits in the same database (version 1, exportSchema = true). Sync state per file is outside the Reminder row.

Hard delete exists, via ReminderDao.deleteById. It is used only by FullBackupManager.restore to replace the set. Every other deletion is an isArchived tombstone, so rows absent from a backup vanish without a tombstone.
updatedAtEpochMillis is overwritten with the current time on every repository create and update. Sync conflict detection compares this field. There is no version counter or per-field clock.
